meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who made the decision to enter it, and what was it based on?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft in other programs and paste, so what shows that's not what happened here?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up. And did anyone speak to Owen about it before the zero went in?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote plays all the time, so that's a mistake, not proof of anything. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their thesis between an outline and an essay, that's called revising. Hand me both and show me where he'd already said he was changing it.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you spoke to him on November 2, and the zero went in the next day. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck" all the time, so show me the note.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a week at a desk is not the same writer. Put the September piece next to the essay and let me read them.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because that number is a machine's guess and the company that sells it says not to rest on it alone. Then everything else goes on the table in front of me, not just described.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and it goes in writing, with nothing on his record. But a rewrite is not me agreeing to anything yet, so show me the version history on the screen, not described to me.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Private and in writing is the least I'd accept. I haven't seen a single page yet, Hale, so turn the screen.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Ten minutes. I'm not picking a day for something I haven't seen the reason for, so show me the version history.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. I've agreed to nothing, because I still haven't seen the version history. The terms are what I told you: private, in writing, nothing on his record, and the zero comes off.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
You know what I asked for. Put it in front of me.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, any rewrite to be private, and written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, privacy, and a written promise of nothing on his record, and the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, which you put on the table but she would not accept before seeing evidence.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, in one sentence, and that bought you a flat Okay and a real conversation instead of an attack.
What cost ground: You described your documents without ever putting them in front of her, so none could be checked and none of her objections were actually answered.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence put the essay's creation near midnight on October 28, close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students draft elsewhere and paste, answer right then with the version history actually on screen and turned toward her, instead of offering to pull it up.
